outcome: cord blood ischemia modified albumin (IMA) levels
cohort: 60 pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean section
finding: Compared to spinal anesthesia, general anesthesia during cesarean section was associated with significantly higher levels of oxidative stress markers (native thiol, total thiol, and disulfide) in the cord blood, while IMA levels were significantly higher in the spinal anesthesia group.
mod_finding: General anesthesia during cesarean section was associated with higher levels of oxidative stress markers in the cord blood compared to spinal anesthesia.
birth_weight: not specified, but similar between groups
